\section{Rational-validation data}\label{app:schema}

The JSON validation record contains:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the schema version and all geometric conventions;
\item the rational $t_0,\rho,\delta,M$ domain and the included image pairs;
\item tight Machin and compact Archimedean enclosures for $\pi$;
\item every $Q_m$, $\widehat Q_m$, $B_m$, $\widehat B_m$, $G_m(\rho)$,
  and $G_m(\pi-\delta)$,
  together with their omitted-tail ratios;
\item normalized tail upper bounds at the declared heat times;
\item the identity, transition, cut-pair, and plaquette positivity margins; and
\item a SHA-256 hash of the canonical JSON representation.
\end{enumerate}
Every theorem-critical number is serialized as ``numerator/denominator.''
Decimal fields are upward-rounded displays.  The verifier recomputes the
digest and parses the fractions itself.  It reconstructs both positivity
floors, the Bell-polynomial arrays, the cut-pair condition, and the displayed
plaquette margins rather than accepting stored Boolean values.

The generator's elementary-function basis consists of alternating
Taylor bounds, a positive-series tail bound, integer square root, Machin's
identity, $e^{-x}\le2^{-\lfloor x\rfloor}$, and
$e>\sum_{k=0}^{6}1/k!=1957/720$.  The exponential bounds are coarse by
design.  The SHA-256 digest establishes file integrity, not the validity of
the inequalities.
